summary: I added a dormant listing failpoint to Core. It lives in static members `FailListingOf` and `ListingError` on the existing `SynchronousIoCancel`. `DirectoryReader.List` consults it with the folder's path and a page number right after each query returns, before the error check, so the keep-earlier-pages and flag-Unreadable path runs unchanged. The window hook arms it by reflection in `Initialize`, before the app's Main, from `FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING=<name>|<page>|<error>`. It logs 'armed', and 'fired' each time it fails a listing; a bad value is logged and thrown, so the app exits 0xE0434352 before its window opens. Two new window cases prove it. T-007 reads the tree through tree mode's WALK: Q (2,000 files, listed first) is read in full; P fails at page 2, keeps 355 of 2,000 files, reads 'could not be read in full', opens onto exactly those 355 rows, each drawn by its own container, more than the viewport holds; R, denied outright, reads 'could not be opened'. T-008 feeds four bad values. Two new mutants in WindowMutants.ps1 show T-007 fails when the name check is removed and when the Core member is missing. The full window suite (48 cases), the 414 Core tests, rules-parity and a real run of the published exe all pass.

files.why: The listing failpoint: static FailListingOf (checks the name, page >= 2, error not 0 or 18, and an optional fired callback) and ListingError (swaps in the error for the named folder's Nth page, only when Windows returned a page). Following O-010, these are static members on the existing class rather than a new static class.

Read passes the folder's path to a private List overload, which counts pages and runs each query result through SynchronousIoCancel.ListingError before its `error != 0` check. The public List(handle, fullClass), used for the root, passes no path, so the root is never faulted.

ArmFailListing parses FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING, reaches SynchronousIoCancel.FailListingOf by reflection before Main, and logs 'fail-listing armed/fired/refused'. Initialize throws the refusal on purpose, so a bad value ends the app before its Main. The header docs are updated.

Adds New-PartwayTree, T-007 (the partly-read row beside Q read in full and R denied) and T-008 (four bad FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING values). Both are registered in ValidateSet, HookedCases and All; FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING is added to HookVariables; the header comment is updated.

Adds mutants ListingFailsAnyFolder (the failpoint's name check removed, per review M1's 'settle it by running') and NoFailListingMember (FailListingOf renamed, so reflection finds nothing). Each must make T-007 fail for its own reason.
Replaces the sentence that recorded the partly-read row as untestable with a pointer to SL-082's failpoint and to T-007 and T-008.

obligations.how:
T-007 arms FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING='

|2|995' for a folder in the fixture. It asserts that exactly one 'fail-listing armed

page 2 error 995' line exists and is the log's first line, ahead of the hook thread's 'loaded mode=tree'. It also asserts that the 'fired' line comes before the 'ending' line. Passed.

T-008 feeds four bad values, each in its own report-mode launch: two parts instead of three, a non-numeric page, page 1, and error 0. It asserts exit 0xE0434352 within 30 s, no report written, and that the hook's single log line is a refusal with the expected reason. Passed. The 'Core member reflection can't find' shape cannot come from an environment value, so the NoFailListingMember mutant in WindowMutants.ps1 feeds it: T-007 then fails on its first check, with 'refused reason=MissingMethodException' and exit 0xE0434352 (mutant run passed).

New-PartwayTree gives P and Q 2,000 files each, with 46-character names (184 bytes per record, about 355 per 64 KiB page), so each listing spans six pages. The fault lands on page 2, and T-007 asserts the 'fail-listing fired

page 2' line under its own message. Measured: P kept 355 of 2,000.
T-007 asserts that P's drawn note is exactly 'could not be read in full' and that 0 < childCount (355) < 2000. It also asserts P's size and on-disk figures equal childCount × 4 KiB. Passed.

Q (a-<tag>) sorts first, and the scanner visits folders in listing order, so Q is listed before P. It has P's multi-page shape. T-007 asserts Q has no note, has an expander, has 2,000 children, and has size and on-disk equal to 2000 × 4 KiB. The ListingFailsAnyFolder mutant (name check removed) makes T-007 fail on Q and on the failpoint firing twice. Mutant run passed.

R is created empty and denied through the existing Deny-Listing (icacls RD) route. T-007 asserts R's drawn note is 'could not be opened', no expander is drawn, childCount is 0 and on-disk is 0. The deny is undone in finally.

With FSA_HOOK_WALK=2, tree mode opens P through its container, as its expander does, and brings every child into view before reading it. T-007 asserts P's container is expanded and that exactly 355 child rows were read, each drawn by its own container, each one of P's own 4 KiB files, with distinct names. It also asserts 355 × 20 px exceeds the 284–330 px viewport, so the count is P's, not the screen's.

No schema-1 change was made (see deviations), and the existing suite was re-run in this tree anyway. `WindowCases.ps1 -Case All` passed all 48 cases: the 46 existing ones plus T-007 and T-008. N-001 to N-004 were not run because they need -IncludeNetwork.

Built as review M1 asked: Q has P's 2,000-file multi-page shape and sorts first, so it is listed first, and T-007 asserts its full child count and size. The 'settle it by running' step became a repeatable mutant: ListingFailsAnyFolder removes the name check. T-007 then fails exactly on 'the failpoint fired once, on P' (fired on a-… and p-…) and on 'Q … was read in full' (Q childCount 355).

Following the M2 disposition, this uses tree mode's tree-row lines, not the schema-1 report. For each root row they carry childCount, size, onDisk and the drawn note and expander; P's realized child rows are counted separately (355 drawn = childCount). T-007 asserts P.size ÷ 4 KiB = childCount, 0 < childCount < 2000, realized rows = childCount and more than the viewport holds, root.size = P.size + Q.size, and the root's rows in on-disk order Q, P, R.

Settled as the m3 disposition says: tree-row lines carry the note, drawn expander, expanded state, childCount and size for every root-level row (Q, P, R and the root), and the case asserts all of them. No per-row names or figures were added to window.FolderTree, keeping Q-016 (WindowReport.cs:91-93).

P and Q have 2,000 files each; the page size is worked out from the record size in the case's comment. The failpoint reports each firing through its callback; the hook logs 'fail-listing fired <name> page <n>', and T-007 fails with its own message ('the failpoint fired: P's listing reached a second page …') when that line is missing. K = 355 ≤ 1000, so WALK opens P; this is also asserted.

The accepted half is done: T-008 is the bad-value sub-case, asserting a non-zero exit (0xE0434352) within the timeout, no report file, and the hook's refusal line. The Disarm/IDisposable half was explicitly not taken by the m7 disposition, so the failpoint has no disarm; this is listed under not_built.

The invariant is reworded where the tree states it, in SynchronousIoCancel.FailListingOf's doc comment: 'The product reads no flag or environment variable that arms it, and never calls this: arming it takes code injected into the process … It ships dormant, not compiled out … so it is no boundary against code already running in the process.' Enforcement already exists in fitness.yaml:312-320 (src/** must not match FSA_HOOK_) and in the SL-082 rule for App. A grep over src finds 0 hits for either. The design document's own invariant text is not in this repository, so I could not edit it here.

deviations: Failpoint location: the design names DirectoryReader.FailListingOf. It was built as static members FailListingOf and ListingError on the existing SynchronousIoCancel class, as O-010's discharge directs ('do not create a new static class … one more static member on the existing SynchronousIoCancel'). The check runs in DirectoryReader.List, which knows the folder's path and the page, right after io.Query returns and before `if (error != 0)`. That is the same position relative to keep-earlier-pages and LastCallAborted as OverrideQueryError. The App-side fitness pattern `FailListingOf\(` still names it.

FailListingOf takes an optional fourth parameter, Action<string,int>? fired. It reports the name of the folder actually failed and the page, so the hook can log the 'fail-listing fired' line that review m4 asked for. The contract listed three parameters.

FailListingOf refuses more than the contract lists (page < 2, empty name). It also refuses a name containing a path separator and win32Error 0 or 18 (ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES), because either value would make a truncated listing look complete.

'Page' means the Nth query call of one listing, counted per listing. The fault replaces only a call that returned a page (0), so a listing that ends before page N is untouched, as the contract says. The scan root is never faulted, because it is listed through a handle with no name.

The design's component 'Tree rows in the window report' (src/FsAnalyser.App/WindowReport.cs) was not built. The M2 and m3 dispositions moved the row evidence to tree mode's tree-row lines, and WindowReport.cs:91-93 keeps row names and figures out of the report (Q-016). WindowReport.cs is untouched and schema 1 is unchanged.
No FSA_HOOK_TREE_EXPAND: tree mode's existing WALK (FSA_HOOK_WALK=2) opens P, as the m6 disposition says.

The bad-value run launches in report mode under the hook's size mode, not tree mode. A wrongly armed hook would then let the app write a report and exit 0, which the case would catch. The exit is the runtime's unhandled-exception code, 0xE0434352, measured here, not a code the hook picks; fitness forbids the hook from calling Environment.Exit. The hook header's 'nothing it does can end the host' is amended to name this one deliberate exception.

The review's 'build once with the name check removed' became a repeatable WindowMutants.ps1 mutant (ListingFailsAnyFolder). A second mutant (NoFailListingMember) feeds the missing-member shape, which no environment value can express.
not_built: Schema-1 report fields for tree rows (WindowReport.cs). The M2 and m3 dispositions replaced them with tree mode's tree-row lines, and Q-016 keeps row names and figures out of the report.
A Disarm() or IDisposable scope for the failpoint (m7's second half). The disposition did not take it, because only the single hook process arms it in this slice.
FSA_HOOK_TREE_EXPAND. The m6 disposition found that WALK already opens the row.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release
tests.note: 0 warnings, 0 errors. The hook also built cleanly into artifacts/window-hook.

Ran three times, the last after a republish from the final source. 'armed' is the first log line, then 'loaded mode=tree', then one 'fired p-<tag> page 2', then 'ending'. P kept 355 of 2,000: note 'could not be read in full', 355 child rows drawn against a 284–330 px viewport. Q is 2,000/2,000 with no note; R reads 'could not be opened' with no expander; root = P + Q = 9,646,080 bytes; walked 359 rows, 0 unrendered.

All four bad values exit -532462766 (0xE0434352) with no report. The only log line is the refusal: FormatException twice, ArgumentOutOfRangeException for 'page' and for 'win32Error'. No WER prompt; each launch ended within about a second.
414 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (27 s). Includes TopLevelRowTextTests, which still uses OverrideQueryError, and ArchitectureRulesTests.

AGREE: 12 facts <- 16 twinned entries, 29 patterns; 47 settled entries not compared. Separate greps found 0 hits for: the src/** seam patterns (FSA_HOOK_, StartupHook, FsaWindowHook, tests/window), FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING or FailListingOf( in App, the BCL File./Directory. pattern in Scanning, and the hook's Environment.Exit, Shutdown, ExitCode= and `using FsAnalyser`.

Exit 0. PASSED: all 46 existing cases (C-001..C-014, O-016, L-001..L-003, B-001..B-008, V-001, P-001, T-001..T-004, T-006, K-001..K-003, R-001, S-001..S-009) plus T-007 and T-008. NOT RUN: N-001..N-004, which need -IncludeNetwork.

With the name check removed, T-007 failed exactly on 'the failpoint fired once, on P' (fired on a-<tag> and p-<tag>) and on 'Q … was read in full' (Q childCount 355). This proves the sibling check catches an unkeyed failpoint.
With FailListingOf renamed, the hook logged 'fail-listing refused reason=MissingMethodException', the app exited 0xE0434352, and T-007 failed on its first check only.
Real run of the published single-file exe, no hook, on this worktree: EXIT 0, Completed, 6,952 files and 962 folders, 1.0 GB, 'Finished: …SL-082'; FolderTree visible with 13 realized and full rows.

follow_ups: The failpoint's static state has no disarm (the m7 half that was not taken). If a Core.Tests Fact ever arms it, it would fault parallel tests that list a folder of the same name, so scope it then.

T-008 asserts the runtime's unhandled-exception exit 0xE0434352 for a startup-hook throw. On a machine with WER's UI enabled, a crash dialog could hold the process until the 30 s timeout. It did not happen here, where every launch ended within about a second.

FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING is armed only when FSA_HOOK_MODE is also set, because Initialize returns early without a mode. This is documented in the hook header; a case that sets only the failpoint variable would get an unfaulted scan, but T-007's first check would fail it.
